title: Practising one memory can make a related one harder to recall
body: In a 1994 study, people learnt words in groups such as fruit. When they practised recalling only some of a group's words, unpractised words from that group were harder to recall later with the category as a clue.
takeaway: When reviewing related terms, rotate which ones you practise so a few familiar answers do not dominate.
source: Anderson, Bjork and Bjork, Journal of Experimental Psychology (1994)

title: A larger turn took longer to picture in a mental rotation test
body: In a 1971 experiment, people judged whether drawings showed the same three-dimensional shape from different angles. Responses typically took longer as the angle between the two views increased.
takeaway: How long a task takes can reveal something about the mental work a person is doing unseen.
visual: two matching angular block shapes shown at different orientations

title: Motivation and incentives predict different parts of performance
body: In a 2014 review of studies spanning four decades, intrinsic motivation was a stronger predictor of work quality, while incentives were a better predictor of quantity.
takeaway: If you reward the amount produced, check whether the work's quality moves in the same direction.
source: Cerasoli, Nicklin and Ford, Psychological Bulletin (2014)
